results.content: The inequality and regressive nature of inflation showed up clearly in the August consumer attitude surveys. The University of Michigan’s preliminary consumer sentiment index plunged 7.6% to 51.0 from 55.2 in July, ending two months of improvement. Expectations deteriorated more sharply than assessments of current conditions, while year-ahead inflation expectations edged up to 4.3%.
results.title: No relief from inflation in July

## Mohamed A. El-Erian's post

### Mohamed A. El-Erian

14 August at 09:38  ·

Key Takeaways from this morning’s UMich US Consumer Sentiment Survey:

The preliminary August consumer sentiment index fell to 51.0 (down from 55.2 in July), well below the consensus forecast of 55.0.

Cost-of-living worries contributed to the decline, with survey director Joanne Hsu citing "notably large reductions… among older consumers, lower-income consumers, and those without a college degree."
